facts.claim: Later school start times are linked to better overall developmental outcomes, longer sleep duration, and less negative mood.
facts.quote: There is converging evidence that later SSTs are associated with better overall developmental outcomes, longer sleep duration, and less negative mood.

facts.claim: The quality of the body of evidence regarding the effects of later school start times is very low because most studies were rated as being at high or unclear risk of bias.
facts.quote: Overall, the quality of the body of evidence was very low, as we rated most studies as being at high or unclear risk of bias with respect to allocation, attrition, absence of randomization, and the collection of baseline data.

facts.claim: Reduced sleep duration was significantly higher in morning-shift students than in afternoon-shift students.
facts.quote: Reduced sleep duration was significantly higher in morning-shift students.

facts.claim: The prevalence of reduced sleep durations (average weekly sleep duration, SDweek <8 h) was higher in morning-shift students (almost 80%) than in afternoon-shift ones (34%).
facts.quote: the prevalence of reduced sleep durations (average weekly sleep duration, SDweek <8 h) to be higher in morning-shift students (almost 80%) than in afternoon-shift ones (34%).

facts.claim: Later school start times are linked to lower levels of sleepiness for high school youth compared to middle school youth.
facts.quote: Later SSTs were more strongly associated with lower levels of sleepiness for high school (versus middle school) youth

facts.claim: Later school start times promoted longer sleep duration over 1 week in one study, but that study had a high risk of bias.
facts.quote: Later school start times promoted longer sleep duration over 1 week (1 study, high risk of bias).

research.angle: While some evidence links later school start times to longer sleep and better outcomes, the quality of the research is often low or the results are limited by bias.
research.verdict: The evidence suggests a link between later school start times and improved sleep for adolescents, but the data is inconsistent and often of low quality.
research.caveat: Many of the studies cited have a high or uncertain risk of bias, making it difficult to be confident about the actual effects of later school start times.
